'''Burgh de Rott''' is a desolate town located in the south-western coast of [[Morytania]], known for housing the [[The Myreque|human resistance to the oppressive vampyres]]. Players must have started [[In Aid of the Myreque]] in order to access the town.

==Transportation==
Several teleports bring players into or close to Burgh de Rott, listed here with their arrival destination. From closest to farthest:

* {{Plink|Morytania legs 3}} — entrance to the town. Requires {{SCP|Diary}} [[Morytania Diary|hard Morytania diary]].
* {{Plink|Mort'ton teleport}} — [[Mort'ton]] town centre, slightly north of Burgh de Rott.
* {{Plink|Barrows Teleport}} — Barrows, north-east of the town.
* {{Plink|Drakan's medallion}} — [[Ver Sinhaza]], from which players can run to the [[Icyene Graveyard]] and take the boat to town.
* {{plink|Minigame teleport|pic=Minigame icon}} — [[Shades of Mort'ton (minigame)|Shades of Mort'ton]] entrance north of the town. Usable once every 20 minutes.
* {{Plink|Fairy ring|pic=Fairy ring (Construction) icon}} {{Fairycode|bip}} — the island east of the [[Mage Training Arena]]. Requires 50 [[Agility]].

==History==
{{LoreSources|In Aid of the Myreque}}

Little is known about Burgh de Rott's history, but it can presumably be dated back to some time in the [[Third Age]] during the vampyre invasion of [[Hallowvale]] due to the [[dusty scroll (In Aid of the Myreque)|dusty scroll]] that can be found amongst some rubble in the town. Whether it was abandoned or destroyed during [[Lowerniel Drakan]] and his [[vampyre]]s' invasion is unknown.

In recent times the town has become a place for human refugees, who have escaped from the vampyres' tyranny. The town is in ruins and the vampyres assume it is uninhabited and thus never go there. During [[In Aid of the Myreque]], the [[player character|player]] helps fix up some of the essential parts of the town, improving the living conditions for the residents. The fact that the town is populated was discovered by [[Gadderanks]], who, accompanied by two [[Vampyre Juvinate]]s, came to tithe the population. The player, however, managed to defeat Gadderanks and the vampyres, meaning that Burgh de Rott is safe for now.

==Locations==
[[File:In Aid of the Myreque - repairing furnace.png|thumb|The Burgh de Rott furnace.]]

=== Buildings ===
Most of the buildings in the town are in complete disrepair. Several still function however:
{| class="wikitable"
!Building
!Description
|-
|[[Aurel's Supplies]]
|The general store, which sells players items. To access the general store you must repair it first using 6 [[plank]]s and 24 [[nails]]. After repairing it players must stock it with 10 [[bronze axe]]s, 3 [[tinderbox]]es, and either 10 [[mackerel]] or 10 [[snail]]s.
|-
|[[Burgh de Rott bank]]
|Allows players to access the [[Bank of Gielinor]].
|-
|[[Myreque's Rest]]
|A run-down pub, featuring a cellar to the town's [[Myreque Hideout#The Burgh De Rott Hideout|Myreque Hideout]]. After the quest [[The Blood Moon Rises]], the pub is revived by [[Veliaf Hurtz]].
|-
|Ruined Building
|North-east of the town, a ruined building filled with rubble can be found. During [[The Blood Moon Rises]], the rubble is cleared, revealing the entry to an old vampyrification lab where the [[Wyrd]] is fought.
|}

===Skill training spots===

* All the [[fishing spots]] in Burgh de Rott necessitate the use of either a [[big net]] or [[harpoon]], making this town nearly as convenient as [[Catherby]] for training [[Fishing]]. There also is a [[small fishing net]] spawn location in a ruined house east of the docks.
* This town has the fifth-closest [[furnace]] to a [[Burgh de Rott bank|bank]], behind [[Port Phasmatys]], [[Shilo Village (location)|Shilo Village]], [[Edgeville]] and [[Neitiznot]].
* There is a [[Fermenting Vat]] located in the [[Myreque's Rest]] cellar after completing [[The Blood Moon Rises]].

=== Other ===
The [[Temple Trekking]] [[minigame]] is available in Burgh de Rott if you have completed In Aid of the Myreque.

==Trivia==
*Most town inhabitants have a common Romanian name.
*[[wiktionary:Burgh|Burgh]] means "city" in French, and rott is an exaggeration of "rot", which means Burgh de Rott translates to "City of Rot".
